targets.authors: Swain S., Alexander J. and Weinberg J.M.
targets.title: The Instability of Philosophical Intuitions: Running Hot and Cold on Truetemp.
targets.evidence_quote: We tried to replicate Swain et al. findings in three experiments: one devised in Polish, and the other two conducted in English.
targets.outcome_quote: We found no priming effect for knowledge ratings regarding the Truetemp case – laypersons were similarly likely to attribute knowledge in all three investigated conditions (primed with a clear case of knowledge, primed with a clear case of nonknowledge, and not primed). These three failed replication attempts are not decisive as to whether the priming effect in question occurs, nevertheless, the collected data puts Swain et al. conclusions about instability of epistemic intuitions in jeopardy.
targets.outcome_reasoning: All three attempts are explicitly described as failed. Caution about conclusiveness is not a verdict of an uninformative attempt.

reasoning: Three new-sample experiments test Swain et al. Background Wright and Weinberg studies are discussed but not themselves targets. Single target paper; its DOI is not printed in the reference.
